metadata.hardware: Apple M3 desktop macOS; not physical phone
metadata.percentiles: Nearest-rank P50/P99. Each board N=20 => P99 is observed maximum, not a robust population tail estimate.
metadata.boards: Every included query has3 distinct original puzzles, each5 warmups +20 measured calls. No permutation-generated duplicates.
metadata.measurement: Independent specified-result queries; family enumeration + exact-type filtering includes its full cost. No first-result substitution.
metadata.comparability: Java rows are search-only; JS/.NET supplement rows include native evidence. Different inputs/runtimes/scopes: do not rank engines by raw finder timings.
metadata.limitations: Limited implementations and partial families retain explicit scopes. Supplemental related queries are not substituted for Wiki targets. 1-shot internal nested probes have no P50/P99 and are excluded.

java.hardware: Apple M3, arm64 macOS, desktop Java; no physical phone measurement

method.fixtureSelection: Prefer two successful states from distinct original puzzles and one negative state from a third original puzzle; accepted negative boards have <=60 filled cells and >=60 candidate entries. Fallback coverage is explicit.
method.percentiles: Nearest rank: sorted[ceil(p*N)-1] for both P50 and P99; N=20 board and N=60 aggregate imply P99 is the observed maximum.
method.sourceIndependence: Distinct SHA256(original 81-digit puzzle) prefixes; no permutation/symmetry-generated fixtures. Multiple states from one source puzzle never count as multiple independent boards.
method.cache: Fresh producer/finder on every call; grid load and initialization outside timing; solver search caches cannot make repeated calls a cached replay.
method.included: Actual next-hint search or explicitly marked complete family enumeration plus exact actual SolutionType filtering. No shared-scanner first-hint substitution.
method.excluded: JVM cold start, input conversion, static dispatcher initialization, proof HTML/JSON, IPC/network, frontend rendering.
method.timeouts: 5s individual search ceiling; raw censored records retained and affected P99 left null instead of discarding timeout samples.
method.samplingLimit: Purposive representative boards, not random puzzle sampling or worst-case bounds; 20 samples cannot estimate population P99 robustly.
method.warmupLimit: Five warmup calls; JVM JIT/GC/system noise remains visible.
method.phoneLimit: Desktop Java timings cannot predict actual mobile JS/WASM or backend end-to-end latency.

supplements.quantiles: nearest-rank: P50=sorted[9], P99=sorted[19] for n20. P99 is maximum, not a reliable 1% tail estimate.
supplements.selection: At least3 independently sourced original puzzles for every query; no manufactured digit/row/column permutations; each original uniquely solved independently of the timed detector
supplements.soundness: Every selected snapshot preserves all givens, the independently checked unique solution and legal candidate masks. Every returned placement/elimination is checked against that unique solution; C# checks all25 calls in harness. This is selected-fixture soundness, not a global correctness proof.
supplements.timingCaveat: Different runtimes and evidence construction scopes; do not rank engines by these numbers. Concurrent host tasks were not isolated. Warm direct finder latency, not browser/network/end-to-end latency.
supplements.rejectedInputs: Classic9 full solve replays on two official Tridagon initial puzzles produced a non-target elimination inconsistent with the known solution. Those solve paths were rejected; no snapshots from them appear here. Only explicitly checked selected detector steps are retained.
supplements.reproduction: run.mjs / bench-tech.mjs for TS; bench-classic9.mjs for Classic9; ResearchBench.cs and selected JSONs for C#. See pinned repositories and configuration diffs.
